SK hynix (000660.KS) said on the 29th during its second-quarter earnings conference call that it is developing new NAND product families such as "near-GPU storage" driven by key-value (KV) cache offloading. "We are proceeding with NAND development in a direction that most efficiently delivers the performance customers require," the company said. [...] KV cache is temporary data required for graphics processing units (GPUs) to handle AI computations. As AI data surges, the high-bandwidth memory (HBM) capacity for storing KV cache is reaching its limits. In response, SK hynix plans to develop new products that mount high-capacity NAND products near the GPU, allowing them to serve as an additional KV cache repository. results.content: The problem lies in the "key-value (KV) cache" — working data that AI stores so it does not have to recompute results it has already calculated. As AI agent services spread, the KV cache grows sharply in scale, deepening the concerns of companies. The industry projects that demand for KV cache will reach up to 100 exabytes (EB, or 1 billion GB) next year, double to 200 EB the following year, and expand to 1 zettabyte (ZB, or 1 trillion GB) by 2030.
